en: be tight against; stick closely to

examples.ko: 아이가 무서워서 엄마 품에 꼭 밀착해요.
examples.en: The child is scared and clings tightly to the mother's chest.

examples.ko: 마스크가 얼굴에 밀착하면 숨 쉬기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If the mask fits tightly against your face, it is hard to breathe.
This film stuck well to the screen.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 몸을 밀착한 채 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The two people took a photo pressed close together.

examples.ko: 지역 주민에게 밀착해서 일하는 가게가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many shops that work closely with local residents.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 몸에 밀착하는 소재라서 운동할 때 좋아요.
examples.en: This outfit is made of a close-fitting fabric, so it is good for exercising.

explain: '붙다'보다 틈 없이 딱 맞닿는 느낌이 강해요. 몸·화면·피부 같은 표면에 쓰고, '지역에 밀착한 가게'처럼 관계가 아주 가깝다는 뜻으로도 써요. 보통 '~에 밀착하다' 꼴로 써요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than 붙다: there is no gap at all. It is used for surfaces like the body, a screen or skin, and also for very close relationships, as in a shop close to its community. It usually appears as '~에 밀착하다'.

examples.en: Our company placed a new order for parts.

examples.ko: 재고가 떨어지기 전에 미리 발주해야 해요.
examples.en: You need to place the order in advance, before the stock runs out.
The goods we ordered yesterday will arrive tomorrow.

examples.ko: 식당 사장님이 매일 아침 재료를 발주해요.
examples.en: The restaurant owner orders ingredients every morning.
We did not order any office supplies this month.

examples.ko: 공장에 책상 백 개를 발주할 거예요.
examples.en: We are going to order a hundred desks from the factory.

explain: 물건을 사는 회사나 가게가 공급하는 곳에 주문을 넣을 때 써요. 개인이 인터넷에서 사는 건 보통 '주문하다'라고 해요. 반대로 주문을 받는 쪽은 '수주하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when a company or shop places an order with a supplier. When an individual buys something online, people usually say 주문하다 instead. The side that receives the order is 수주하다.

examples.ko: 광장 복판에 큰 나무가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A big tree stands in the middle of the square.
The car suddenly stopped in the middle of the road.
The ball rolled toward the middle of the playground.

examples.ko: 접시 복판을 비워 두고 가장자리에 소스를 뿌렸어요.
examples.en: I left the center of the plate empty and drizzled sauce around the edge.
The middle of the lake is the deepest part.
There is an old well in the middle of the market.

explain: '한가운데'와 뜻이 비슷한 말이에요. 앞에 '한-'을 붙인 '한복판'이 더 자주 쓰여요. 보통 '장소 + 복판에' 꼴로 써요.
explain_en: It is close in meaning to 한가운데. The form 한복판, with 한- added in front, is used more often. It usually appears as 'place + 복판에'.

examples.en: The two companies made a contract in secret.
The teacher secretly prepared a birthday party.
Please carry out this work in secret.
The two people who had been meeting in secret got married.
The two countries held talks in secret.
The letter that was sent secretly arrived today.

explain: 거의 항상 '비밀리에' 꼴로 써요. '몰래'보다 딱딱하고 계획해서 숨기는 느낌이라 뉴스나 회의에서 자주 들려요. 친구끼리 장난스럽게 숨길 때는 '몰래'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the form 비밀리에. It is more formal than 몰래 and suggests a planned secret, so you hear it in news and meetings. For playful secrets between friends, 몰래 sounds more natural.

examples.en: The city cut this year's culture budget.
The company said it would cut employees' pay.

examples.ko: 비용을 삭감하면 서비스가 나빠질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you cut costs, the service may get worse.
The government is going to cut next year's subsidies.
We cut the advertising budget and decided to focus on online.
Where does the money from the cut budget go?

explain: 예산·월급·비용처럼 정해진 돈의 양을 줄일 때 써요. '줄이다'는 아무 때나 쓰지만 '삭감하다'는 윗선에서 결정해 깎는 느낌이라 뉴스와 회사 글에 많아요. 반대말은 '증액하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when a fixed amount of money, such as a budget, pay or cost, is reduced. 줄이다 works in any situation, but 삭감하다 feels like a decision made from above, so it is common in news and company writing. The opposite is 증액하다.

examples.en: Thanks to the lawyer, we won the trial.

examples.ko: 이번 승소는 회사에 큰 도움이 됐어요.
examples.en: This court win was a big help to the company.
Everyone was happy to hear the news of the win in court.
The chance that we will win the case is not high.
If you win the case, you can receive compensation.

examples.ko: 작은 가게가 대기업과의 소송에서 승소를 거뒀어요.
examples.en: A small shop won its lawsuit against a large corporation.

explain: 반대말은 '패소'예요. 소송이나 재판에서만 써서 일상 대화에서는 드물고, 뉴스에서 '~이 승소했다'로 자주 들려요. 시합이나 게임에서 이기는 건 '이기다', '승리하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is 패소. It is used only for lawsuits and trials, so it is rare in everyday talk, but you often hear '~이 승소했다' in the news. For winning a match or a game, use 이기다 or 승리하다.

en: be enthusiastic; go wild with excitement

examples.en: The fans went wild over the singer's song.
People are crazy about World Cup games.
The concert hall was noisy because of the cheering audience.
The children will be thrilled with the new toy.

examples.ko: 요즘 젊은 사람들이 이 드라마에 열광해서 매주 챙겨 봐요.
examples.en: Young people these days are so into this drama that they watch it every week.

examples.ko: 우승 소식에 열광한 사람들이 거리로 나왔어요.
examples.en: People who were ecstatic about the victory news came out onto the streets.

explain: '좋아하다'보다 훨씬 크게, 여러 사람이 함께 흥분해서 환호하는 느낌이에요. 보통 '~에 열광하다'로 쓰고, 혼자 조용히 좋아할 때는 어울리지 않아요. 비슷한 '환호하다'는 소리를 지르는 행동에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It is much bigger than 좋아하다: many people get excited and cheer together. It usually appears as '~에 열광하다' and does not fit quietly liking something alone. The similar 환호하다 focuses on the act of cheering out loud.

examples.ko: 힘든 시간을 인내하면 좋은 날이 와요.
examples.en: If you endure the hard times, good days will come.

examples.ko: 오랜 시간 동안 아픔을 인내해 왔어요.
examples.en: I have borne the pain for a long time.

examples.ko: 선수는 부상을 인내하고 경기를 끝까지 뛰었어요.
examples.en: The player put up with the injury and played the match to the end.
You have to be very patient to raise a child.
They say that people who endure eventually succeed.

examples.ko: 더는 인내할 수 없어서 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: I could not stand it any longer, so I got angry.

explain: 말할 때는 '참다'를 많이 쓰고, '인내하다'는 글이나 연설에서 쓰는 조금 딱딱한 말이에요. 명사 '인내'는 '인내심'이라는 말로 더 자주 보여요. '인내심을 가지다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: In speech people mostly say 참다; 인내하다 is a slightly stiff word for writing and speeches. The noun 인내 is more often seen as 인내심. A common phrase is '인내심을 가지다'.

examples.en: The police held back the crowd that was rushing in.
The guard stopped us, so we could not go inside.
I turned back after being stopped by the guard.
My friend tried to stop me, but it was no use.

examples.ko: 아무 제지 없이 건물에 들어갈 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I was able to enter the building without anyone stopping me.
Despite the teacher's attempt to stop them, the children kept chattering.

explain: '말리다'는 일상에서 누군가의 행동을 말릴 때 쓰고, '제지하다'는 경찰·경비원처럼 막을 힘이 있는 사람이 막을 때 자주 써요. '제지를 받다', '제지를 당하다'처럼 쓰고, 막는 쪽은 '제지하다'예요.
explain_en: 말리다 is the everyday word for talking someone out of an action, while 제지하다 is often used when someone with authority, like police or a guard, stops people. You say '제지를 받다' or '제지를 당하다' for being stopped, and 제지하다 for the one stopping.

examples.en: Grades are the only measure for judging a student.
The yardstick of happiness is different for each person.

examples.ko: 온도는 더위를 알려 주는 쉬운 척도죠.
examples.en: Temperature is an easy measure of how hot it is.

examples.ko: 물가는 경제 상태를 보는 중요한 척도로 쓰여요.
examples.en: Prices are used as an important gauge of the state of the economy.

examples.ko: 돈을 성공의 척도로 삼는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people take money as the measure of success.

examples.ko: 친구를 사귀는 데 나이는 척도가 아니에요.
examples.en: Age is not a standard when making friends.

explain: '기준'은 판단할 때 대 보는 선이고, '척도'는 정도를 재는 자 같은 것이에요. '행복의 척도'처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것을 잴 때 많이 써요. '~의 척도가 되다', '~을 척도로 삼다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: 기준 is a line you hold something up against to judge it; 척도 is more like a ruler for measuring degree. It is often used for things you cannot see, as in 'a measure of happiness'. Common patterns are '~의 척도가 되다' and '~을 척도로 삼다'.

examples.en: I deduced the culprit from the evidence.

examples.ko: 문맥으로 모르는 단어의 뜻을 추론할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can infer the meaning of an unknown word from the context.
It is hard to infer the cause from this result alone.

examples.ko: 그림 속 단서로 이야기의 끝을 추론해 보세요.
examples.en: Try to work out the ending of the story from the clues in the picture.

examples.ko: 글의 내용을 추론하는 문제는 시험에서 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Questions that ask you to infer the content of a text often appear on exams.
Let's check whether what we inferred is right.

explain: '짐작하다'는 대충 느낌으로 맞히는 것이고, '추론하다'는 근거에서 논리적으로 끌어내는 것이에요. 읽기 시험의 '추론 문제'가 바로 이 말이에요. 보통 '~로 ~을 추론하다' 꼴로 써요.
explain_en: 짐작하다 is a rough guess based on a feeling, while 추론하다 means drawing a conclusion logically from evidence. The 'inference questions' in reading tests use this word. It typically appears as '~로 ~을 추론하다'.

en: become stagnant; fall into a slump

examples.en: The economy slumped, so the shop's customers decreased.

examples.ko: 분위기가 침체돼서 아무도 말을 안 했어요.
examples.en: The mood sank, so nobody said anything.

examples.ko: 침체된 도시를 살리기 위해 축제를 열어요.
examples.en: They hold a festival to revive the stagnant city.
If the economy stays in a slump for long, jobs decrease.
I sold the shop before the market went into a slump.
It seems that sales will keep stagnating.

explain: 경제·시장·분위기처럼 전체가 활기를 잃고 가라앉았을 때 써요. 사람 기분이 가라앉을 때는 '우울하다'가 더 자연스러워요. '침체하다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when something as a whole, such as the economy, a market or a mood, loses energy and sinks. For a person's feelings, 우울하다 sounds more natural. There is also the form 침체하다.

examples.en: The president sent a special envoy to the United States.
The special envoy arrived at the airport yesterday.
I was chosen as a special envoy to attend the peace talks.

examples.ko: 특사는 두 나라 사이의 문제를 의논했어요.
examples.en: The envoy discussed the problems between the two countries.
I delivered a letter to the envoy who was dispatched abroad.

examples.ko: 이번 특사 파견은 아주 중요한 일이에요.
examples.en: Sending the envoy this time is a very important matter.

explain: '대사'는 한 나라에 오래 머무는 외교관이고, '특사'는 특별한 임무를 위해 잠깐 보내는 사람이에요. '특사를 파견하다', '특사를 보내다'로 자주 써요. '평화 특사'처럼 앞에 임무를 붙여요.
explain_en: A 대사 is a diplomat who stays in a country for a long time, while a 특사 is sent for a short time on a special mission. Common phrases are '특사를 파견하다' and '특사를 보내다'. The mission can be put in front, as in '평화 특사'.

en: dean (of a college within a university)

examples.en: The dean of our college is very kind.
The dean gave a congratulatory speech at the graduation ceremony.
A new person has come as dean of the art college.
I asked the dean about scholarships.
I made an appointment for a meeting with the dean.

examples.ko: 그분은 학장이 되기 전에 오랫동안 교수였어요.
examples.en: Before becoming dean, that person was a professor for many years.

explain: '총장'은 대학 전체의 우두머리이고, '학장'은 공과대학·인문대학 같은 단과대학의 우두머리예요. 직접 부를 때는 '학장님'이라고 해요. 고등학교의 우두머리는 '학장'이 아니라 '교장'이에요.
explain_en: A 총장 heads the whole university, while a 학장 heads one college inside it, such as engineering or humanities. When addressing the person directly, say 학장님. The head of a high school is a 교장, not a 학장.

examples.en: I am unhappy with the verdict, so I am preparing an appeal.

examples.ko: 항소는 판결이 나온 뒤 정해진 기간 안에 해야 해요.
examples.en: An appeal has to be filed within a set period after the ruling.
The lawyer explained the grounds for the appeal.

examples.ko: 항소가 받아들여져서 재판을 다시 하게 됐어요.
examples.en: The appeal was accepted, so the trial is being held again.
The company accepted the ruling without an appeal.
New evidence is important in this appeal.

explain: 1심 판결 뒤에 하는 것이 '항소'이고, 2심 뒤에 대법원에 하는 것은 '상고'예요. 보통 '항소를 하다', '항소를 제기하다'로 쓰고, 동사로는 '항소하다'를 써요. 뉴스와 법 이야기에서만 나와요.
explain_en: An appeal made after a first trial is 항소; one made to the Supreme Court after the second trial is 상고. It is used as '항소를 하다' or '항소를 제기하다', and the verb form is 항소하다. It appears only in news and legal talk.

examples.en: The prosecutor did not accept the ruling and appealed.
The result felt unfair, so I decided to appeal.
To appeal, you have to submit the documents first.
The company will appeal within a week.
A person who has appealed goes through the trial again.
Even if you appeal, the result may be the same.

explain: 1심 판결에 불복할 때 '항소하다'를 쓰고, 2심 뒤에 대법원으로 가는 건 '상고하다'예요. 보통 '판결에 항소하다'처럼 써요. 뉴스에서 '항소했다'로 자주 들려요.
explain_en: You 항소하다 when you do not accept a first-trial ruling; going to the Supreme Court after the second trial is 상고하다. It is used like '판결에 항소하다'. In the news you often hear '항소했다'.

examples.en: The Grand Canyon is a very large canyon.
A clear river flows between the canyon walls.
We walked along the gorge.

examples.ko: 협곡 위에 긴 다리가 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A long bridge stands over the canyon.

examples.ko: 깊은 협곡에서 바람 소리가 크게 들렸어요.
examples.en: The sound of the wind was loud in the deep gorge.
When it rains, the gorge becomes dangerous.

explain: '골짜기'는 산 사이의 낮은 곳을 두루 부르는 말이고, '협곡'은 좁고 깊고 벽이 가파른 곳이에요. 보통 큰 계곡이나 관광지를 말할 때 써요. 동네 뒷산의 작은 골짜기에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: 골짜기 is a general word for a low place between mountains, while 협곡 is narrow and deep with steep walls. It is usually used for large valleys or tourist sites. It is not used for a small valley on a local hill.

examples.en: I have longed for freedom for a long time.
The child yearned for the parents' love.
People prayed, longing for peace.
The dream I had yearned for finally came true.

examples.ko: 성공을 갈망하는 사람은 쉽게 포기하지 않아요.
examples.en: A person who craves success does not give up easily.
I long for a chance to study in Korea.

explain: '바라다'나 '원하다'보다 훨씬 간절하고 목마른 느낌이에요. 자유·사랑·평화처럼 크고 추상적인 것에 자주 써요. 일상의 물건에는 '갖고 싶다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is far more intense and thirsty than 바라다 or 원하다. It is often used for big, abstract things such as freedom, love and peace. For everyday objects, 갖고 싶다 sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 인간의 광기를 보여 줘요.
examples.en: That movie shows human madness.
I could sense madness in that person's eyes.
War drives people into frenzy.

examples.ko: 광기와 천재는 종이 한 장 차이라는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a saying that madness and genius are separated by a thin line.
Everyone was startled by the frenzied laughter.

examples.ko: 점점 광기에 빠져 가는 주인공이 무서웠어요.
examples.en: The main character who was sinking deeper into madness was scary.

explain: '미친 짓'처럼 일상에서 나무라는 말과는 달라요. '광기'는 이성을 잃은 상태나 보통 사람이 이해하기 어려운 격한 마음을 가리키는 글 속 말이에요. '광기 어린', '광기에 사로잡히다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It differs from everyday scolding phrases like 미친 짓. 광기 belongs to written language and points to a state of lost reason or an intense feeling that ordinary people cannot understand. Common forms are '광기 어린' and '광기에 사로잡히다'.

examples.ko: 구강 건강을 위해 하루 세 번 이를 닦아요.
examples.en: I brush my teeth three times a day for oral health.
I had an oral checkup at the dentist.

examples.ko: 구강이 건조하면 입에서 냄새가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If your mouth is dry, your breath can smell.

examples.ko: 구강 청결제는 입안 냄새를 줄여 줘요.
examples.en: Mouthwash reduces odor in the mouth.

examples.ko: 아기가 물건을 구강에 넣지 않게 조심해요.
examples.en: I am careful not to let the baby put things into the mouth.

examples.ko: 음식을 씹는 동안 구강에서 소화가 시작돼요.
examples.en: Digestion begins in the mouth while you chew food.

explain: '입'은 일상 말이고 '구강'은 입 안쪽을 가리키는 의학·건강 쪽 말이에요. 치과·보건 이야기에서 '구강 검진', '구강 청결제'처럼 다른 말과 붙여 써요. 평소에는 '구강이 아파요'보다 '입이 아파요'라고 해요.
explain_en: 입 is the everyday word, while 구강 is a medical and health term for the inside of the mouth. It is attached to other words in dental and health talk, as in 구강 검진 and 구강 청결제. In daily life people say '입이 아파요' rather than '구강이 아파요'.

en: belong to; revert to; be vested in

examples.en: Ownership of this land belongs to the state.
The invention made at work became the property of the company.

examples.ko: 계약이 끝나면 건물이 주인에게 귀속된다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the building goes to the owner when the contract ends.
All the profit will go to the school.
Check where the copyright belongs.
Property that has been vested is used for the public.

explain: 재산·권리·책임이 어느 한쪽의 것이 될 때 쓰는 법률·계약 쪽 말이에요. 보통 '~에 귀속되다'로 쓰고, 일상에서 물건이 누구 것이 되는 건 '~의 것이 되다'라고 해요. 서류와 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a legal and contract word for when property, rights or responsibility become one party's. It usually appears as '~에 귀속되다'. In daily life, for an object becoming someone's, people say '~의 것이 되다'.

examples.en: Concentrated juice is drunk after mixing it with water.
A lot of water is lost during the concentration process.
I mixed the concentrate into warm water and drank it.
When the concentrating is done, the solution becomes much thicker.
Herbal medicine made by concentrating comes in a small amount.

examples.ko: 이 세제는 농축 제품이라 조금만 써도 돼요.
examples.en: This detergent is a concentrated product, so you only need a little.

explain: '농축 주스', '농축액', '농축 세제'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 자주 써요. 같은 뜻을 일상에서는 '진하게 하다'로 풀어 말해요. 동사로는 '농축하다', 저절로 되면 '농축되다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is often placed before another noun, as in 농축 주스, 농축액 and 농축 세제. In daily speech people say '진하게 하다' for the same idea. The verbs are 농축하다 for doing it and 농축되다 for when it happens by itself.

examples.en: As the water reduces, the broth becomes concentrated.

examples.ko: 맛이 농축돼서 한 숟가락만 먹어도 진해요.
examples.en: The flavor is so condensed that even one spoonful tastes rich.
Nutrients are concentrated inside the fruit.
If you boil it for a long time, the broth begins to concentrate.
When the solution is concentrated, its color gets darker.
It is a book in which long experience has been distilled.

explain: 저절로 또는 어떤 과정으로 진해질 때 쓰는 피동 형태예요. 음식뿐 아니라 '경험이 농축된 책'처럼 많은 것이 한곳에 모였다는 비유로도 써요. 사람이 일부러 할 때는 '농축하다'예요.
explain_en: This passive form is used when something becomes stronger on its own or through a process. Besides food, it is used figuratively, as in 'a book where experience is distilled'. When a person does it on purpose, use 농축하다.

examples.en: The juice factory concentrates fruit juice.
I concentrated the solution by evaporating the water.

examples.ko: 여행 이야기를 한 권에 농축할 거예요.
examples.en: I am going to condense my travel stories into one book.
If you boil it down for a long time, the flavor gets deeper.
The concentrated liquid must be kept in the refrigerator.
They study methods of concentrating nutrients.

explain: 물을 빼서 진하게 할 때, 또는 긴 내용을 짧게 줄여 핵심만 담을 때 써요. '용액을 농축하다', '내용을 농축하다'가 흔해요. '요약하다'는 말을 줄이는 것이고 '농축하다'는 알맹이를 진하게 모으는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used both for removing water to make something stronger and for squeezing long content down to its core. '용액을 농축하다' and '내용을 농축하다' are common. 요약하다 shortens the words, while 농축하다 feels like gathering the essence into a denser form.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 작은 가게를 모태로 시작했어요.
examples.en: That company started out from a small shop as its origin.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 전통 민요에서 모태를 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can find the origin of this song in traditional folk songs.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 작은 야학이 모태가 되었어요.
examples.en: A small night school became the origin of this school.

examples.ko: 모태에서 아기가 자라는 동안 엄마의 목소리를 들어요.
examples.en: While growing in the womb, a baby hears the mother's voice.

examples.ko: 지금의 도시는 작은 항구 마을을 모태로 커졌어요.
examples.en: The present city grew out of a small port town.
The source of this culture is rural life.

explain: 원래 뜻은 엄마의 배 속이지만, 요즘은 어떤 것이 생겨난 바탕을 말할 때 더 많이 써요. '~를 모태로 하다', '~를 모태로 삼다'로 자주 써요. 비슷한 말 '뿌리', '바탕'보다 격식 있게 들려요.
explain_en: Its original meaning is the mother's womb, but today it is used more for the base from which something grew. Common patterns are '~를 모태로 하다' and '~를 모태로 삼다'. It sounds more formal than the similar 뿌리 or 바탕.

examples.en: Hot gas erupts from the volcano.
The discontent held in for so long burst out all at once.
There is a place where hot spring water gushes from the ground.
When magma erupts, the surroundings become dangerous.
The moment the emotion burst out, tears came.

examples.ko: 가스가 분출될 때 큰 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: A loud noise came when the gas was released.

explain: 물·불·가스·감정이 안에서 세게 밖으로 나올 때, 저절로 일어나는 일이면 '분출되다'를 써요. 사람이나 기계가 일부러 내보내면 '분출하다'예요. '불만이 분출되다'처럼 감정에도 써요.
explain_en: When water, fire, gas or emotion comes forcefully out from inside, and it happens by itself, use 분출되다. When a person or machine sends it out on purpose, use 분출하다. It also works for feelings, as in '불만이 분출되다'.

examples.en: The volcano spewed black smoke.
This fountain shoots water high into the air.
People began to vent the discontent they had held back.
Let out your energy through exercise.
There is a hole that releases gas from underground.

examples.ko: 간헐천은 일정한 시간마다 뜨거운 물을 분출한다고 해요.
examples.en: They say a geyser shoots out hot water at regular intervals.

explain: 물·가스·불꽃처럼 안에 있던 것을 세게 밖으로 내뿜을 때 써요. 감정을 풀어낼 때도 '분출하다'를 쓰지만 입말에서는 '터뜨리다'가 더 흔해요. 피동 '분출되다'와 짝이에요.
explain_en: It is used when something inside, such as water, gas or flames, is blown out forcefully. It can also be used for letting emotion out, though 터뜨리다 is more common in speech. It pairs with the passive 분출되다.

examples.en: The mother is nursing the baby.

examples.ko: 밤마다 수유 때문에 잠을 잘 못 자요.
examples.en: I cannot sleep well because of night feedings.

examples.ko: 수유 중에는 약을 먹기 전에 의사와 의논해요.
examples.en: While breastfeeding, talk to a doctor before taking medicine.
There are more shopping malls with nursing rooms.
If breastfeeding is hard, it is fine to give formula.

examples.ko: 아기가 밤에 두 번 수유를 해요.
examples.en: The baby is fed twice at night.

explain: '젖 먹이다'는 입말이고 '수유'는 병원·육아 글에서 쓰는 말이에요. '수유하다', '수유 중', '수유실'처럼 붙여 써요. 젖병으로 먹일 때도 쓸 수 있지만 '모유 수유'가 가장 흔해요.
explain_en: 젖 먹이다 is the spoken form, and 수유 is the word used in hospitals and parenting writing. It is attached to other words, as in 수유하다, 수유 중 and 수유실. It can also be used for bottle feeding, but 모유 수유 is the most common.

examples.en: My grandmother is recuperating in the countryside.

examples.ko: 수술 후에 한 달 동안 집에서 요양했어요.
examples.en: After the surgery, I recuperated at home for a month.
I recuperate in the mountains to regain my health.
You have to take a break from work while you recuperate.
Thanks to a long recovery, I got much better.

examples.ko: 몸이 나을 때까지 병원에서 요양할 거예요.
examples.en: I will recuperate in the hospital until I get better.

explain: '쉬다'는 가벼운 휴식이고, '요양하다'는 아프거나 수술한 뒤 몸이 낫도록 오래 조용히 지내는 거예요. 보통 '시골에서 요양하다', '집에서 요양하다'처럼 장소와 같이 써요. 노인을 돌보는 시설은 '요양원'이에요.
explain_en: 쉬다 is a light rest, while 요양하다 is staying quietly for a long time so that the body can heal after an illness or surgery. It is usually used with a place, as in '시골에서 요양하다'. A facility that cares for the elderly is a 요양원.

examples.ko: 이번 달에는 잉여 자금이 조금 생겼어요.
examples.en: This month some surplus funds came up.

examples.ko: 회사의 잉여 인력을 다른 부서로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: The company moved its surplus staff to another department.
Surplus farm products are sometimes sold at a low price.
I saved the surplus that was left over after spending.

examples.ko: 잉여가 생기지 않도록 주문량을 잘 맞춰요.
examples.en: We adjust the order amount well so that no excess builds up.

examples.ko: 잉여 예산은 다음 달로 넘기기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to carry the excess budget over to next month.

explain: 필요한 만큼 쓰고도 남은 것을 말해요. '나머지'나 '남은 것'은 일상 말이고, '잉여'는 경제·회사 글에서 '잉여 인력', '잉여 생산물'처럼 써요. 인터넷에서는 할 일 없는 사람을 놀리는 말로도 쓰니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It refers to what is left over after using what was needed. 나머지 and 남은 것 are everyday words, while 잉여 appears in economic and business writing, as in 잉여 인력 and 잉여 생산물. Online it is also used to tease someone with nothing to do, so be careful.
